corrections.source_says: The Ns correctly reproduce Model 3 regression observations at the proposal-PI-field-year level. Proposals can contribute multiple rows, so these are not distinct-abstract or people counts. Retain the Ns with this explicit composite-unit qualification; unique-abstract counts for these analysis samples are not stated and should be null if separately recorded.

corrections.source_says: Add within-investigator topical distance: cosine distance to the investigator's own proposals in the previous two years within the same agency. This separate output-scored novelty outcome shows no clear association with LLM involvement in either private dataset. Figure S50 plots coefficients with investigator-clustered 95% confidence intervals but prints no exact coefficients, standard errors, interval endpoints, or N; record figure_only and leave those numbers null.
corrections.quote: In other words, proposals with higher LLM involvement are not systematically farther from an investigator’s own prior proposals.

corrections.source_says: Describe SPECTER2 average cosine distance and mention robustness variants, as form-spec rule 7 requires: the prior-two-year window, L2 and raw cosine distances, alternative reference models and preprocessing, AI-vocabulary exclusion, length restrictions, investigator-status controls, standardized predictors, and single-field analyses. Public awards also have field/subagency checks. The stylistic-rewriting check is calibration, not randomized people. Gemini-based distinctiveness results are explicitly not statistically significant.
corrections.quote: For example, in the semantic distinctiveness analysis, the Gemini-based 𝛼estimates yield no statistically significant results.

confirmed: The source is arXiv:2601.15485v3 [cs.DL], 5 Jul 2026, marked Forthcoming in PNAS; title and six authors match. The PDF has 97 pages and is not the journal version of record (PDF p. 1).

The whole markdown conversion was read, including appendices and references. Supporting Information begins on p. 15; Figures S1-S54 and Tables S1-S15 are included (PDF pp. 15, 26-94; references pp. 95-97).

No randomized people study appears; all four main datasets are observational. Random selection is of calibration abstracts (PDF pp. 3, 5, 12-13, 15, 17). There is no small randomized experiment to assess against the 50-person rule.
Private corpora contain 1.6K NSF and 4.1K NIH proposal submissions from two US R1 universities, including funded, unfunded and pending proposals with starts in 2021-2025 (PDF p. 12).

Public corpora contain 57K NSF and 74K NIH awards with starts in 2021-2025 (PDF p. 13). Corpus counts are not people counts; no investigator total is given, so participant counts appropriately remain null.

The main analysis covers starts in 2023-2025: average SPECTER2 cosine distance to the same agency's prior-year funded abstracts, converted to within-year percentiles from 0 to 100 (PDF pp. 5, 16, SI S1.2).
GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 generates reference rewrites, not a verified record of grant writers' models. Alpha estimates LLM-modified sentences and ranges from 0 to 1 (PDF pp. 3, 15-17).

Every coefficient, SE, significance marker, N, and Model 3 R2 in the four reported strings matches Tables S1-S4 (PDF pp. 80-83). Model 3 Ns are 1886/8198/60283/56413 and R2 values are 0.72441/0.53894/0.78893/0.86886, in dataset order.

Tables S1-S4 control log(funding): Model 1 has no listed fixed effects, Model 2 adds start-year/field effects, and Model 3 adds investigator effects. SEs are clustered by investigator; * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001 (PDF pp. 80-83).

The text reports approximately 5 percentile points lower distinctiveness for NSF awards and 4 for NIH awards from the 25th to the 75th percentile of LLM involvement; all four main associations are negative and conditional, not causal (PDF p. 5).

This is not a synthesis and reports no pooled meta-analytic estimates. Main predictors are unstandardized; Table S13 standardizes predictors to z-scores while retaining the percentile outcome (PDF p. 24, SI S2.16; p. 92).
summary: This is observational evidence with no randomized people study; the recorded source version and table statistics are correct. Corrections address the analysis unit, omitted outcome and robustness details, incomplete fields, and rounded summary coefficients.
